title: Cocktail 2 Closes Its First Weekend at ₹44 Crore. Shahid Kapoor's Rom-Com Is the Comeback Nobody Bet On.
excerpt: A mixed-review opener that grew every single day, crossed ₹85 crore worldwide, and already buried Shahid's last film. Now comes the hard part — surviving Akshay Kumar's jungle on Friday.
body:
The numbers came in on Monday morning and the trade rooms in Mumbai did a small double-take. **Cocktail 2** — written off by half the critics before the first interval — had done the one thing a fragile rom-com almost never does in 2026. It grew. Every. Single. Day.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=XXxUqLHq1xg</youtube>

Friday opened at roughly ₹12.5 crore nett. Saturday climbed past ₹15.5 crore. Sunday peaked at ₹16.25 crore. Add it up and the **Homi Adajania**-directed sequel walked out of its opening weekend with about ₹44 crore nett in India and a worldwide gross that has already sailed past ₹85 crore. For a film carrying the weight of a fourteen-year-old cult classic and a fresh cast nobody asked for, that is not a polite start. That is a statement.

https://x.com/ruhani8990/status/2068712542114025877


![Shahid Kapoor — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/25/Shahid_Kapoor_at_Bloody_Daddy_launch_%28cropped%29.jpg)



> **"Add it up and the **Homi Adajania**-directed sequel walked out of its opening weekend with about ₹44 crore nett in India and a worldwide gross that has already sailed past ₹85 crore."**



> "There is a message in this film. Nowadays, the kind of relationships, situationships and questions around commitment that are going on — there's a very relevant, rooted message at the end of the movie." — Kriti Sanon, to ANI

Let's be honest about what this is. **Cocktail 2** is not a continuation of the 2012 original that gave us **Deepika Padukone** at her loosest and most luminous. It's a spiritual successor — same Maddock house, same Pritam soundtrack DNA, same urban-heartbreak instinct — but a clean slate. And the slate belongs to three people who needed this win badly.

Start with **Shahid Kapoor**. After *O Romeo* limped to an ₹8.5 crore opening day in February and *Deva* topped out at a lifetime of ₹34 crore, the chatter around him had curdled into the worst thing you can say about a leading man: *reliable, not bankable.* Cocktail 2 crossed Deva's entire lifetime gross before Saturday night. It is now, by trade estimates, his third-biggest opener ever. The man didn't need a reinvention. He needed a hit. He got one.

Then there's **Rashmika Mandanna**, who continues her quiet annexation of the Hindi box office, and **Kriti Sanon**, who notched her second-biggest post-pandemic opener after *Crew*. The chemistry the trailers promised — that prickly, flirtatious triangle the original built its legend on — apparently landed. Word of mouth is doing the heavy lifting now, and word of mouth is the only currency that makes a film *grow* into its weekend instead of bleeding out of it.


![Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg)


The diaspora story is where it gets interesting. Overseas, Cocktail 2 has pulled somewhere between ₹19 and ₹26 crore depending on whose tracker you trust — a chunky slice of that ₹85-crore worldwide pile. This is the genre NRI audiences in New Jersey, Wembley and Brampton actually show up for: glossy, song-stuffed, set in the kind of aspirational metropolitan India that plays beautifully on a Friday night out. Romance travels. It always has.

Not that the original's ghost will let anyone relax. **Cocktail** (2012) opened at a modest ₹10.5 crore and rode goodwill all the way to roughly ₹74 crore nett — a number that, adjusted for today's ticket prices, would be monstrous. The sequel has the faster start. Whether it has the legs is the ₹74-crore question.

And the legs are about to be tested. On Friday, **June 26**, the genteel rom-com crowd gets bulldozed by **Akshay Kumar's** ensemble riot **Welcome To The Jungle** — forty-odd stars, a ten-acre jungle set, and the kind of mass-comedy noise that swallows screens whole. Cocktail 2 needed every rupee of this weekend's momentum, because come Friday it's fighting for shows.

For diaspora viewers who can't catch it in theatres, the patience play is the OTT window — Maddock's recent titles have tended to land on **Netflix** or **JioHotstar** within roughly eight weeks of release, so a late-summer streaming drop is the safe bet. Confirmation hasn't dropped yet; when it does, your living room gets the cocktail.

For now, though, the toast belongs to the theatres. A film everyone was ready to bury just had the best weekend of Shahid Kapoor's recent career. Pour another.
